text: First and foremost, it is important to differentiate the term absorption from utilization . From a nutritional standpoint, absorption refers to the passage of nutrients from the gut into circulation. As such, there is virtually no limit to how much protein a person can absorb from a given meal. After digestion, the protein's constituent amino acids traverse the intestinal wall and enter circulation where virtually all become available for use at the tissue level. A potential issue occurs when a person ingests individual free-form amino acids, which can bring about competition for transport through the enterocytes. In this case, amino acids present in the highest concentrations are preferentially absorbed at the expense of those in lesser concentrations (49).
